subject: GoldCrest: BCP/DR evidence & RTO/RPO details request
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@goldcrest-payments.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@goldcrest-payments.com
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: BCP/DR evidence & RTO/RPO for evaluation

Hi Vivek,

We're preparing GoldCrest's operational risk review ahead of our pilot procurement. Our risk team has asked for evidence around Redwood's business continuity and disaster recovery posture specifically focused on measured RTO/RPO and recent DR test artifacts. High-level list of what we need: 

- RTO and RPO numbers (for both Hosted API and Private deployment options) and brief explanation of what each number covers (control plane, data plane, client failover).
- The latest DR test report or run summary (date, scope, outcome) and any follow-up actions.
- An excerpt of the recovery runbook that shows failover steps and roles.
- Any SOC 2 / SIG mapping or attestation that references continuity controls, or a pointer to where we can view it.

We prefer PDF/CSV artifacts and a short one-page cover explaining the key numbers. Can you get this to us by Thursday (2025-07-24)? Our commercial / security review timeline is tight. If there are items we cannot share publicly, let us know and we'll arrange an NDA/subset access.

Thanks,
Jordan Mills
Senior Risk Manager
GoldCrest Payments

---
Note: procurement contact is cc'd for tracking.

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@goldcrest-payments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BCP/DR evidence & RTO/RPO for evaluation

Jordan — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to share the artifacts and a short narrative. To make sure we return exactly what your reviewers need, quick clarifying questions: 

1) Which workload profile should we prioritize? (a) chat/text-generation API (high token throughput), (b) embeddings/async workloads, or (c) both. Recovery characteristics differ slightly.
2) For Private (on-prem/VPC) deployments, do you want our default guidance (what Redwood provides) or only examples from current Private customers (we can redact customer names)?
3) Are you okay with a PDF bundle shared via a secured Drive link and a CSV summary of test metrics? For any restricted logs/artifacts we will request a narrow NDA and provide a time-limited link.

Planned next steps from our side: Marissa will pull the runbook excerpts and test summaries (she owns DR testing), Karthik will assemble the SOC2/controls mapping and any SIG specifics, and I'll coordinate delivery and a short 30-minute walkthrough if you'd like. We can deliver by EOD Thu (24 Jul).

If Thursday is tight, let us know and we can prioritize the RTO/RPO summary first then follow with deeper artifacts.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Solutions Architect (Security & Compliance)
Redwood Inference

---
Vivek: tagging Marissa & Karthik for action.

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@goldcrest-payments.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BCP/DR evidence & RTO/RPO for evaluation

Hi Vivek — thanks. Priorities below: 

- Primary: chat/text-generation API (customer-facing endpoints)
- Secondary: embeddings (background batch jobs)

For hosted API, we need RTO/RPO under two failure classes: 
  A) control plane outage (API gateway / control services) — expectation is recovery fast enough to avoid customer-visible downtime > 30 minutes; please provide measured P95/P99 where available.
  B) data-plane/state failure (replication lag, KV cache lost) — we care about RPO (how much data loss in minutes) and the typical recovery steps to resume traffic.

We would like: 
- a short CSV with RTO/RPO metrics from the last full DR run (date + key metrics),
- runbook excerpt (redact any internal hostnames),
- a one-page cover that states what the numbers mean for production traffic.

Procurement has also requested a signed attestation or a DocuSign envelope if possible — they use that during evaluation. I've added the procurement portal link here for your tracking: https://procurement.goldcrest-payments.com/request/GC-2025-0413

If you can confirm Thursday delivery, we'll slot the documents into our security review.

Jordan
Senior Risk Manager
GoldCrest Payments

---
Jordan: added the DocuSign ask and clarified P95/P99 needs.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@goldcrest-payments.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 24 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: BCP/DR evidence & RTO/RPO for evaluation

Jordan — attaching the bundle we discussed. High-level summary up front: 

- Hosted API (regional failover): typical RTO 10–20 minutes for automatic regional failover (we measure failover completion at ~P95=12 min, P99=22 min in our April 15, 2025 test). RPO for persisted customer data (transactional event streams) is <=1 minute when cross-region replication is healthy; for ephemeral KV cache the effective RPO is "best-effort" (cache rebuild may lead to increased latency until warm-up).

- Private (VPC/on-prem): Redwood provides an operator-run recovery playbook. Baseline guidance: RTO objective typically 2–4 hours for full capacity failover if the customer relies on their own storage snapshots; RPO depends on replication configuration — we document a 15 minute RPO target for recommended active-replication setups. We include an excerpt of the playbook covering control-plane failover and state rehydration.

What we've attached/shared: 
- bcp-dr-evidence-Redwood-Goldcrest-20250724.pdf (one-page cover + executive summary + test conclusions)
- rto-rpo-test-summary-20250415.csv (metrics from the April 15, 2025 full failover exercise; includes P50/P95/P99 and event counts)
- runbook-excerpt-v2.txt (redacted runbook steps for control-plane failover and DB promotion)

Notes and caveats: 
- The April 15 test was a planned regional failover simulation (no customer data was exposed). A small number of follow-up action items were identified (see Appendix A in the PDF); all items were closed by May 6, 2025.
- SOC 2 continuity controls map: Karthik has prepared the mapping; we can either share the full mapping via an NDA-protected link or provide a SOC 2 bridge letter.
- DocuSign: we prepared a short attestation and can route it to your procurement contact — please confirm the signer and email for the envelope.

Next steps: 
- Tell us if you want the SOC2 mapping via secure link (we can provide access by EOD tomorrow).
- If you'd like a quick walkthrough of the test CSV and runbook, we can set a 30-minute call early next week.

Attachments (stubs):
- bcp-dr-evidence-Redwood-Goldcrest-20250724.pdf (application/pdf, 1.1 MB)
- rto-rpo-test-summary-20250415.csv (text/csv, 48 KB)
- runbook-excerpt-v2.txt (text/plain, 12 KB)

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Senior Reliability Engineer (DR & Resilience)
Redwood Inference

---
Marissa: delivering per Vivek's coordination. If procurement needs the DocuSign envelope routed now, tag me and I'll sign the attestation as the DR test owner.
